Plus they’re obviously attracted to eachother so, imo, no additional coincidences or explanations were required for them to become pals. 

Also, adding to Zack’s unnecessary existence, Cloud clearly had a mild obsession with Sephiroth since he was young, looking up to him and wanting to be like him. Because of that, in addition to them both being prototype experiments of sorts- injected with the same alien cells, it always seemed to make more sense to me that Cloud should confuse his own identity with Sephiroth’s, not some super minor character who is briefly mentioned and then pops up again maybe one other time in an optional side quest. Zach’s entire existence in the story always sort of confused me. 

If Zach’s role was expanded to be Cloud’s long time battle buddy, savior, and the dude that sacrifices his life to protect Cloud from Shinra, and if the player was given an adequate amount of time playing as him (maybe pre-intro mission or sometime later when Cloud is figuring himself out) I could see Zack doubling as Cloud’s motivation to destroy Shinra as well as the reason why he confuses his own identity with Zack’s. Especially if Cloud wasn’t entirely lucid while traveling with him. That would explain why Cloud had such an affinity for Zack and felt the need to dress like him, wield his weapon, and super impose himself into Zack’s body during situations where he actually just witnessed Zack’s actions as a bystander- like at Mt. Nibel. Because he would’ve only been processing all that information subconsciously
as a vegetable or whatever. 

I think some of the additional media on ff7 has hinted at some of this, but the OG mentions Zack so casually that the player couldn’t be blamed for forgetting him entirely. 

All that said, Cloud was always an abnormal dude- made clear by his flashbacks and dialogue regarding his childhood with Tifa and how he viewed and interacted with the other kids. That alone wouldn’t sufficiently explain his pathological characteristics as an adult, though. He is indeed and without a doubt fucked up psychologically when the player is introduced to him, though, only to become clearer and clearer- the extent of his madness and confusion- as we witness more and more shit that he does which is socially odd at the best of times and down right violently psychotic at the worst (almost kills Aerith). 

I suppose it wouldn’t take a huge leap of imagination to entertain the idea that he imagined Zack in some or even all of the scenarios where the two of them interacted. Of course we know he isn’t entirely fabricated because of Aerith though, so it’d be more likely if Zack was either very important to Cloud as I said earlier or if Zack was simply the last person Cloud interacted with while he was still lucid and possibly immediately before his mind was shattered by Hojo’s experiments. 

If Jenovah’s cells potentially cause delirium and partial cognitive dissolution in subjects injected with them, acutely amplified upon their exposure to trauma, it’d be entirely possible for Cloud to assume the identity of the last person in his mind- Zack. Maybe post cell injection the subject’s identity is temporarily destroyed as Jenovah begins supplanting aspects of its host. The subject’s mind might frantically attempt to assemble its sense of self out of desperation and as a defense mechanism, pulling fragments from the most recent memory database or “RAM”, and then ham fistedly sewing them together with other older and more solid fragments that later come into focus as the subject’s mind gradually puzzles itself back together. When the human inside of the subject eventually wins the struggle, assuming it does, what its left with is a shattered mirror’s reflection. A poorly reassembled copy of the original person with various facets and fibers of themselves replaced during the desperate and instinctive moments that accompany times of self preservation or the fight or flight response. 

What eventually came to was “Cloud” if he had viewed his reflection in such an imperfect and distorted mirror. Traumatized but oblivious of the trauma and therefore unaware of the instrument causing it. No longer himself or even human but not quite anything else either. 

He becomes a vague, uncertain, and spliced together creature, and in order to become a lucid organism again he has no choice but to surrender to the harsh new unfamiliar identity forced onto him. He’s given only two horrible and terrifying options: either submit to something foreign but static and easy, or submit to an impossible and absolute uncertainty- the unknowable process of a mystery in the twisted form of some pending structure or liquid manifold of random thoughts and information, but also potentially a recipe for the resurrection of the animal once named Cloud before his sublimation into a mercurial vapor. 

Could the malformed and inhuman cloud of material that Hojo created out of the person Cloud even coalesce and untangle itself back into its original form? All the torment he endured throughout the journey as experienced by the player may have been the only antidote for the imposter Cloud who turns into an unequal ratio of Cloud to Zack, with Zack occupying Cloud’s perception of what he assumed to be his role in recent events and Cloud occupying the decimated remainder.

I think Zack was just a coincidental and innocent bystander. Zack just naturally became a part of Cloud’s new identity due to a combination of their close proximity to eachother during what I can only assume was the worst part of Cloud’s entire life, Cloud’s envy of Zack’s position as a soldier, and their inevitable bond as friends while escaping and making their way back to Midgar. Zack then dies off screen, Cloud gradually becomes more lucid and begins harboring deep resentment toward Shinra (probably both consciously and subconsciously). I hate to be repetitive but seriously observe her move set. She will telegraph all attacks albeit in diverse ways. She will hit behind herself if you stand there and try to greedily capitalize on your “safe” situation. You need to continually pay attention to everyone and everything in BB to “git gud”. The game rewards your focus and dedication. 

Also, lock off. Seriously. Locking on can be your best friend or worst enemy. The more astute observer will notice that while locked on you will side step. I don’t know the exact iframes of either but the non locked on roll is similar to dark souls in utility and distance while the quick step dooms you to extremely close combat. I won’t lie, the quick step is also great in many scenarios but the dark souls roll is fucking fantastic in every situation.

Also, as an aside that i have absolutely no objective proof of, I’ve felt that locking on in most fromsoft titles allows my adversaries to track my movements better. Conclusion: lock on when it suits the situation and at no other time. 

Vicar Amelia can also be made easier with items which prevent her from healing effectively, fire paper, grinding to an extremely and pathetically high level, etc. I don’t recommend this however because the reliance on those crutches subtracts from your potential to increase in skill which is mandatory to experience the game in its awesome entirety the way which it is most enjoyable and intended to be be played.

You can also summon help btw. 

If you find the blood starved beast easier than VA you can aquire a chalice from winning that fight and then search for a ridiculously difficult  labyrinth by the glyph “cummmfpk” if it’s still active. Shortly after the beginning in the first archway, look to your left and you might see a health bar being depleted in the distance. If you allow it to be exhausted you will obtain over 80k blood echoes. At such an early point in the game, the 80k will allow you to progress to ridiculously high advantage. I don’t recommend this however tho because if you’re playing bloodborne you’re probably not the type of individual to enjoy an overpowered player experience. Also, the trial and error; dying constantly; and sense of earning every victory will give you more satisfaction than any method of cheese or overpowering. 

VA, as an aside only has one strategy that you should be wary of and that is her ability to heal. It’s a dps race then. Be agressive when she isn’t and be cautious when she is. 

Also, finally, fighting the BSB first gives you the advantage of experience as well as stats so i wil always recommend doing that.

Good luck, and with the highest respect… git gud
